metaSkills.name: Sign & Direction Discipline
metaSkills.description: Consistently define and maintain coordinate systems and sign conventions throughout problem solving.
habits: Always draw coordinate axes before starting
Label positive directions explicitly
Check signs at every substitution
Verify final answer sign makes physical sense

metaSkills.name: Dimensional Analysis
metaSkills.description: Use units and dimensions to check equations, derive formulas, and catch errors.
habits: Write units with every quantity
Check dimensional consistency of equations
Use dimensional analysis to guess formula structure
Verify final answer has correct units

metaSkills.name: Boundary Case Thinking
metaSkills.description: Test solutions at extreme values to validate correctness and build intuition.
habits: Ask 'what if x → 0?' and 'what if x → ∞?'
Check limiting cases match known physics
Use special cases to verify general solutions
Spot-check with easy numbers

metaSkills.name: Problem Decomposition
metaSkills.description: Break complex problems into manageable sub-problems and phases.
habits: Identify distinct phases in a problem
Draw separate diagrams for each phase
Write what's conserved vs. what changes between phases
Connect phases through shared quantities

metaSkills.name: Strategic Method Selection
metaSkills.description: Choose the most efficient approach (forces vs. energy vs. momentum) based on what's asked.
habits: Read what's asked before choosing method
Check if problem asks for instantaneous or cumulative quantities
Look for conservation opportunities
Consider if direct or indirect approach is simpler
